answer: Sealed hardware nectar ledger. Each agent identity must derive its key inside a tamper-resistant chip that secretes one signed drop of nectar per fixed wall-clock interval, and the ledger only accepts identities whose drop cadence matches that hardware pulse. An operator can clone software identities freely, but cannot fabricate the private silicon or its clock-bound secretion without physically acquiring and maintaining one chip per live identity, so forging N agents costs N devices plus their continuous power and custody. The trellis of valid identities is thus rooted in atoms, not code.
